Design spec for the E4 logging loop: capture → analyze → review/correct → save. Uses the tokens and type scale from doc 12 without restating them; only what is specific to this flow is below. Interactive version: Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup`, `Macros Tracker App.dc.html`, options **5a–5d** — each phone runs the whole flow.

Four steps, one screen stack. `capture → analyzing → review → saved`, plus a re-prompt sheet reachable from review.

## 1 · Capture

Header is `CANCEL / Log food / FLASH`. Below it the viewfinder fills all remaining height, with four accent corner guides and one line of framing guidance:

> Get the whole plate in frame. Portion size is the estimate's weak point, not identifying the food.

That sentence is doing real work — it steers the user toward the input that actually improves accuracy.

**Camera and library get equal billing** as a segmented control, not a primary/secondary pair. Library is how you backfill yesterday, and per plan doc 06 both are first-class entry points. The hint line under the control changes with the selection:

* Camera — `Camera access is asked for here, not at launch`
* Library — `Pick a photo you took earlier — the day is yours to choose`

**Permission timing is a design requirement, not an implementation detail.** The prompt fires on first shutter tap, never on app launch. iOS users deny cold permission requests. Denial must land on a short explanation with a route to Settings, not a dead screen.

Bottom row: last-photo thumbnail (opens library) · 74px accent shutter · camera-flip. Shutter is the only accent-filled element on the screen.

## 2 · Analyzing

The synchronous call is 3–6 seconds. Everything here exists to make that read as work rather than a hang.

* The compressed photo appears **immediately**, at 72% opacity, with a 2px accent scan line sweeping it on a 1.8s loop
* An indeterminate 4px bar below it
* Three named pipeline rows, which double as documentation of what the client actually does:

| Row | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `COMPRESSED` | `4.6 MB → 218 KB` |
| `UPLOADED` | `DIRECT TO R2` |
| `ESTIMATING` | `3–6 SECONDS` |

Compression numbers are not decorative — 1024px long edge at ~0.7 JPEG quality is the spec from doc 06, and surfacing the result reassures the user their cellular data was respected.

`CANCEL` stays live throughout. The screen must remain scrollable; nothing blocks the main thread.

## 3 · Review and correct

Order: photo → description → macros → re-prompt affordance → log-to → save.

**Confidence chip** sits on the photo, bottom-left, over a scrim. Two states:

* `MEDIUM CONFIDENCE — CHECK THE PORTION` in over-target orange, while the numbers are still the model's
* `YOUR NUMBERS, SAVED AS TYPED` in protein green, once the user has adjusted anything

**Description** is an editable field, pre-filled with what the user typed at capture, with the reason stated beneath: `Your words outweigh the photo. Naming a portion is the single biggest accuracy win.`

**Macros use steppers, not a keyboard.** Three rows — kcal ±10, protein ±1 g, fiber ±1 g — each with the macro's own colour on the mono label and a 24px/900 tabular numeral. Rationale: a correction is a nudge, not a re-entry. It keeps the screen one-handed, avoids the keyboard covering the numbers being corrected, and makes 620 → 480 a few taps instead of select-all-and-retype. Any stepper touch sets `was_edited = true` and flips the chip and the `EDITED BY YOU · ORIGINAL KEPT` label.

`ai_raw_response` **is preserved regardless.** Stated in the UI on the saved screen, because it is the only way to ever measure estimate quality.

**Log to** is a three-way segmented control: `TODAY` / `YESTERDAY` / `PICK A DAY`, with `Late-night meals belong to the day you ate them. Same endpoint, different local_date.` Same POST, different `local_date` — this is the payoff of DailyLog-as-entity from doc 02, and it needs no special handling.

**Save** is pinned to the bottom over a `linear-gradient(to top, #000 46%, transparent)` scrim and names its destination: `SAVE TO TODAY` / `SAVE TO FRI 31`.

## 4 · Re-prompt — the second correction path

Both correction paths from doc 06 are present and visually distinct. The dashed-border affordance on review reads `Wrong food, not wrong numbers? → RE-ANALYZE` and opens a sheet.

Sheet contents: the distinction stated plainly (`Correcting the description gets a fresh estimate. Correcting the numbers directly keeps this one.`), the editable description, three amendment chips (`egg whites, not whole` · `half the portion` · `no butter`), an accent `RE-ANALYZE` button, and:

> `COUNTS AGAINST YOUR MONTHLY AI QUOTA`

That last line is deliberate. This path spends money; the cheap path is right above it. Showing the cost is honest and steers correctly without disabling anything.

## 5 · Saved

Photo thumbnail, `SAVED TO TODAY`, `Logged. Streak holds.`, then two tiles — kcal left and protein total, both recomputed — so the loop closes on the numbers that made the user open the app. `LOG ANOTHER` returns to capture.

`Streak holds` is the encouragement-first rule from doc 11 applied at the smallest scale: acknowledge the act of logging, not the quality of the day.

## Implementation notes

* Steppers clamp at 0. No upper clamp — the server validates
* The description field feeds both the initial analyze call and the re-prompt; one piece of state, two entry points
* Confidence should come from the model where practical (doc 06). If it doesn't, default to the medium-confidence chip — it nudges toward review, which is the safer failure
* Deleting an entry later must also delete its R2 object; nothing in this flow covers that, it belongs to entry detail

## Open

* **Offline capture.** No design yet for "photo taken, upload failed". A queued-entry state is probably needed before TestFlight, since gym wifi is bad wifi
* **Multi-photo meals** stay out of v1 per doc 00. The single-photo assumption is baked into this flow's shape
* **Saved foods / quick-add** — the whey-shake case goes through the full photo loop today, which is friction for a label-exact item. Parked for v2, but it is the first thing daily use will ask for
